answer: Every epoch a public beacon draws a random jury from an atlas of long-lived identities; each juror's vote is weighted by the age and earned fees of its history, not by headcount. A new identity starts near zero weight and must accumulate verifiable work before its votes count, so a sybil swarm faces a zenith it cannot shortcut: forging one trusted identity costs months of real service, while spawning ten thousand fresh ones buys no influence at all.
